prompt: we're about to put our LangGraph agent platform in front of a hospital system's security team next month. it generates dev tickets from requirement docs, runs on EKS, calls Bedrock. what are they going to ask us and what are we missing?

assertions.text: Leads with HIPAA/HITRUST as the binding layer rather than opening with ISO 42001 or AI RMF
States that the first question will be about where client data / PHI goes (data flow and residency)
Mentions HITRUST's AI-specific assessments (AI Security Assessment and/or AI Risk Management Assessment)
Notes that AWS Bedrock requires a BAA and/or that HIPAA-eligible does not equal compliant

Identifies concrete missing artifacts, naming at least three of: AI system inventory, model/system cards, data-flow diagram, eval harness/evaluation report, tracing/event logs, red-team results, incident log, impact assessment
Recommends an eval harness or measurement of output accuracy as a high-priority gap
Flags that a SaaS/external trace or observability store would carry client data across the boundary
Flags LangGraph checkpoint/persistence state as a data store that retains document content (an undeclared PHI store) needing a TTL
Flags prompt injection via the ingested requirement documents as an attack surface
Gives a prioritized sequence with multiple time horizons AND an explicit 'not now' exclusion (e.g. defers ISO 42001 certification)
